描述_EN: around 1730 ceramic handles were introduced to europe from china. knives have been used since prehistoric times, but the history of knives, forks and spoons for eating in europe probably commenced in the fourteenth century, and their use became accepted by the sixteenth century. throughout the ages artists and craftsmen have made virtuoso carvings as a display of their skill and ingenuity. although cutlers were required by their guilds to be able to make a complete knife, handles of carved ivory, silver, bronze and glass were usually imported or made by specialist craftsmen. although ivory, wood and stone are relatively easy to carve, other materials such as gemstones are much more demanding. ebony, ivory, fish skin, tortoiseshell, amber, bone, horn and shell were all popular for decorating cutlery. this ivory kife-handle is probably made in germany in about 1650. most of these carvings were made for wealthy patrons and collectors, who delighted in the rarity of the material and quality of the carving. until the late seventeenth century it seems to have been common practice for people to carry their own cutlery, often in a leather case.
描述_ZN: 大约在1730年，陶瓷手柄从中国传入欧洲。 刀子从史前时代就开始使用了，但是欧洲的刀子、叉子和勺子吃饭的历史可能开始于十四世纪，它们的使用在十六世纪就被接受了。 历代艺术家和工匠都以精湛的雕刻来展示他们的技能和智慧。 虽然行会要求刀匠能够制作一把完整的刀，但象牙、银、青铜和玻璃雕刻的刀柄通常是进口的或由专业工匠制作。 虽然象牙、木头和石头比较容易雕刻，但其他材料如宝石的雕刻要求更高。 乌木、象牙、鱼皮、玳瑁、琥珀、骨、角和贝壳都是装饰餐具的常用材料。 这个象牙刀柄可能是1650年左右在德国制造的。 这些雕刻品大多是为富有的赞助人和收藏家制作的，他们对材料的稀有性和雕刻的质量感到高兴。 直到十七世纪末，人们携带自己的餐具似乎是一种普遍的做法，通常是放在一个皮箱里。
